headline: Shark trapped for a month in South Korean canal is finally freed
standfirst: Bukang-i successfully guided out after month in which it drew 1.6m visitors and was watched over by YouTubers In South Korea, they call them jagyeongdan, a word whose meaning sits somewhere between vigilante group and…
body_markdown:
Bukang-i successfully guided out after month in which it drew 1.6m visitors and was watched over by YouTubers In South Korea, they call them jagyeongdan, a word whose meaning sits somewhere between vigilante group and neighbourhood watch. Each night they put on hi-vis vests, picked up their selfie sticks and gathered around the harbour in Busan to keep watch over an unlikely charge: a stranded shark affectionately known as Bukang-i. On Wednesday, after more than a month in the canal and at the third attempt, the shark was successfully guided out, South Korea’s oceans ministry said. (The Guardian Asia)

**BBC News Asia** adds: Early on Thursday morning local time, South Korea's oceans ministry said the shark had been successfully guided out of the canal.

**The Straits Times Asia** adds: The authorities launched the third attempt to lead her out of the canal on the morning of Oct 21.

**Bangkok Post** adds: SEOUL - A shark that has become a viral sensation in South Korea was coaxed out of a canal in which it was stuck, authorities said on Wednesday, as falling temperatures raised concerns for its survival.

**The New York Times** adds: The 10-foot-long dusky shark, nicknamed “Bukangi,” was successfully guided back to the open ocean after a third rescue attempt.

This digest was assembled automatically from reporting by The New York Times, BBC News Asia, The Globe and Mail, Bangkok Post, The Guardian Asia and The Straits Times Asia. Follow the source links below for the full coverage.
